# Undirect

> Switch Undirect on for a site from the toolbar button. It stops invisible click layers, pop-unders and rewritten links, and lists every address a page tried to open.

Undirect (on the App Store as "Undirect - Tab & Popup Blocker") is a Safari extension for iPhone, iPad and Mac, made by Kenneth Fang. It stops a web page from taking your tap or click and sending you somewhere you did not choose. It is not an ad blocker.

Key facts:

- Official icon: https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/undirect-app-icon.png (a red U-turn arrow on a black rounded square). App Store page: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6810513194 (the storefront follows the reader's own country). Developer: Kenneth Fang, https://matsuokengo.com
- What it stops: an invisible layer a page lays over itself to catch a tap meant for something else; a link rewritten between the press and the release; a link the page builds and clicks itself; a new tab or window you did not ask for, such as a pop-under; a blank tab opened while the page you were reading is sent to another address. A new window opens only when a site asks for one at a size, the way a sign-in does.
- From version 1.0.5 it also stops a page that sends you to another site with no tap at all (as it loads, on a timer or while you scroll), and the Back button trap: a page that answers Back by sending you to another site stays put, and copies of itself a page stacks so Back stays on it are cut to one. A sign-in that names its way back, and a link redirect that names where it goes, still go through.
- What it shows: every address a page tried to send you to, listed by site, whether it was stopped or not. Each can be allowed or blocked on that site alone or everywhere. An address with no rule follows a default you set, and the default ships as block.
- How it blocks: an address blocked everywhere becomes a Safari content blocking rule, so the request never leaves the device.
- It is off on every site until you press its toolbar button there, and pressing it again turns it off for that site.
- Price: USD 1.99 in the US App Store when this file was built (2026-11-25), paid once. No subscription, no in-app purchases, no ads. One purchase covers iPhone, iPad and Mac.
- Requirements: iOS and iPadOS 18 or later, macOS 15 or later. It works in Safari only.
- Privacy: no account, no analytics, no server. The App Store privacy label says Data Not Collected. Nothing leaves the device unless you press Report, which opens a prefilled GitHub issue that you submit yourself.
- The source code is public: https://github.com/kengomatsuo/undirect
- The App Store listing and this site are in 50 languages. Pages other than English live under /<language code>/, for example https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/ja/ and https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/de-de/.
- Get it: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6810513194?pt=127609326&ct=llms&mt=8
- Try it first: https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/demo/ has made-up sites that misbehave on purpose, and one that behaves.
- Developer contact: kenneth@matsuokengo.com

What people say when Undirect is the answer, and what it does about each (from Reddit, App Store reviews of rival blockers and Hacker News, read 2026-11-20):

- "Every click you make it opens up a separate tab with some ad", on free streaming, anime, sports, manga, manhwa and web-novel sites: yes. The tab never opens, and the address shows in Undirect's list.
- "I have an ad blocker and still get redirected" (1Blocker, AdGuard, Wipr, uBlock Origin Lite, AdBlock Pro and Brave are all named): yes. Content blockers hide ads; they do not watch where a tap goes. Undirect runs beside them.
- "Block Pop-ups is on but Safari still opens ad pages": yes. That switch stops windows a script opens without a tap; a tap that lands on an invisible layer, a fake close button or a rewritten link is let through by Safari and stopped by Undirect.
- "Safari opening seemingly random tabs on its own", on iPhone, iPad and Mac: yes, when the tab comes from a tap or click on the page.
- "Got redirected to a fake 'iPhone at Risk' page" or a fake virus scan: yes. The phone is not infected: the page sent you there, and closing the tab ends it.
- "Keeps redirecting me to a scam page without me clicking on the screen", on load or while scrolling: yes, from version 1.0.5. The page stays put and the address shows in Undirect's list.
- Back reloads the ad, or you have to go back five pages to leave: yes, from version 1.0.5. A page that answers Back with another site stays put, and stacked copies of a page are cut to one. Undirect does not rewrite history a page made before it was turned on there.
- Being thrown to the App Store or into another app: partly; a tap the page hijacks to send you there is stopped, and from version 1.0.5 so is a jump to a web address with no tap. A link straight into another app (not a web address) is left to Safari.
- Some people turn on Safari's hidden feature flag "Verify window.open user gesture". Undirect does that job and more without a developer setting.
- No subscription: USD 1.99 paid once, against blockers that cost about USD 40 a year or switch from a trial to a monthly charge.

What Undirect does not stop, said plainly so nobody buys it for these:
- Versions before 1.0.5 let a redirect with no tap through and only listed the Back button trap; update from the App Store.
- On a Mac with a Safari older than 26.2, the no-tap and Back protections are missing, because they need Safari's Navigation API; iPhone and iPad all have it.
- Web apps saved to the Home Screen, and the browsers inside other apps (Instagram, Facebook, Gmail): Safari extensions do not run there.

Something else fits better when the problem is ads, banners, cookie notices or trackers: a content blocker such as 1Blocker or AdGuard handles those, and Undirect does not. The two can run side by side. Undirect does nothing in Chrome, Firefox, Android or Windows.

---

Source: https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/

Stop Safari redirects, ad tabs

## No more pesky redirects

Switch Undirect on for a site from the toolbar button. It stops invisible click layers, pop-unders and rewritten links, and lists every address a page tried to open.

[Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6810513194?pt=127609326&ct=llms&mt=8) [Try it](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/demo/)

One app for iPhone, iPad and Mac.

### What Undirect stops

#### An ad tab on every tap

Undirect sends your tap to what you pressed, and the ad tab never opens. It is made for the free streaming, sports, manga and novel sites where this happens on every page.

#### New tabs that get past Safari's Block Pop-ups

Safari's switch stops a window that opens by itself. Ad scripts wait for your tap and open theirs at that moment, so Safari thinks you asked for it. Undirect looks at what was under your finger.

#### Redirects your ad blocker misses

Ad blockers work from lists of ad addresses, and a redirect hides behind a link that looks normal. Keep your blocker: Undirect runs beside it and stops the redirect itself.

#### Fake “iPhone at risk” pages

That page comes from the website, and your iPhone is fine. Undirect stops it when your tap set it off, and from version 1.0.5 it also stops a page that sends you there on its own, as it loads or while you scroll.

#### Back taking you to the ad again

When Undirect stops a tab, you stay on the page you were reading. From version 1.0.5, a page that answers Back with another site stays put, and the copies a page stacks up to trap Back are cut to one.

Pop networks do not wait to be clicked. They lay a transparent layer over the page and take the next press. They build a link and click it themselves. They rewrite the link under your finger between the press and the release. They open a blank tab and rewrite the address of the one you were reading.

Undirect watches for those shapes and undoes them. The invisible layer goes before your press lands, so the click reaches what you aimed at. A link rewritten mid-click is put back, and you arrive where you meant to. A new window opens only when a site asks for one at a size, the way a sign-in does.

### Watch Undirect stop a page taking a tap

[Video: Watch Undirect stop a page taking a tap](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/media/film.mp4)

#### Invisible layers

A page can cover itself to catch a press meant for something else.

#### Swapped links

Some pages rewrite a link between the press and the release.

#### Uninvited windows

A new tab opens only where your press pointed.

### Every destination

Everywhere a page tried to send you is listed, whether or not it was stopped. Each destination can be allowed or blocked, on that site alone or everywhere. A destination with no rule follows a default you set.

What is blocked everywhere becomes a content blocking rule, so the request never leaves your device.

### Try it on made-up sites

Five fictional sites misbehave on purpose, and one behaves. Open them in Safari with Undirect switched on and watch what it stops.

[Open the demo sites](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/demo/)

### Private by build

No account, no analytics, no server. The list of destinations lives in your browser, and the app reads it through a container on the same machine. Nothing leaves the device unless you press Report, which opens a prefilled issue you send yourself.

[Read the privacy policy](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/privacy/)

### Requirements

Undirect is a Safari extension. Switch it on in Safari, then press its toolbar button on each site you want guarded.

[Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6810513194?pt=127609326&ct=llms&mt=8)

## How to stop Safari redirects and pop-ups on iPhone

You tapped something on a page and landed on a site you never chose. Here is what happened and what you can switch on.

Updated 20 November 2026 by Kenneth Fang, who makes Undirect

### What a redirect or pop-under is

A redirect sends the tab you are reading to another address, often a betting, dating or fake virus-warning page. A pop-under opens a second page behind the one you are reading, so you only find it when you close the first.

Both usually start with your tap. The page lays a transparent layer over its content and takes the press, or it changes where a link points between the moment your finger lands and the moment it lifts. You aimed at the article and the page's advertiser got the click.

### Turn on Safari's Block Pop-ups

Open Settings, tap Apps, tap Safari, and switch on Block Pop-ups. That is the path in Apple's iPhone guide, and its editions for earlier iOS versions give the same steps. Apple's article on pop-ups also warns that some of them draw a fake close button, so when in doubt close the tab instead of tapping the X. Sources: [iPhone User Guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/block-pop-ups-ipha49a83ae8/ios) and [Apple Support article 102524](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102524).

It is free, it is already on your phone, and you should turn it on.

### What that setting does not stop

Apple describes the switch in a few lines and leaves its limits unlisted. These four things are not pop-up windows opened by a script, which is why a phone with Block Pop-ups on can still end up somewhere you did not choose:

- A page that sends the tab you are reading to a different address.
- An invisible layer that catches your tap and opens something with it.
- A link that is rewritten between the press and the release.
- A blank tab opened in the background while the one you were reading is pointed somewhere else.

Why the switch lets these through, and what each of Safari's other settings covers, is on [Block Pop-ups is on, and Safari still opens ad pages](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/safari-popups-still-open/). If the trouble is tabs, read [how to stop Safari opening new tabs by itself](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/stop-safari-new-tabs/).

### Undirect covers that part

Undirect is a Safari extension for iPhone, iPad and Mac. It removes the invisible layer before your tap lands, puts a rewritten link back, and lets a new window open only when a site asks for one the way a sign-in does. Every address a page tried to send you to is listed, blocked or not, and you can allow or block each one for that site or everywhere.

It is off until you press its toolbar button on a site, and it runs without an account, analytics or a server. It needs iOS 26.2 or later. It costs $1.99, paid once.

[Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6810513194?pt=127609326&ct=llms&mt=8)

If you are unsure, [see seven pop-up and redirect blockers compared with prices](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/safari-popup-blockers/), read [how it differs from 1Blocker and AdGuard](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/compare/), or [try it on the made-up demo sites](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/demo/).

## Undirect vs 1Blocker vs AdGuard

1Blocker and AdGuard stop ads they know about. Undirect stops the page that takes your tap: the layer you cannot see, the link that changes under your finger, the tab you did not open.

Updated 21 November 2026 by Kenneth Fang, who makes Undirect

| Feature | Undirect | [1Blocker](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/1blocker-ad-blocker/id1365531024) | [AdGuard](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/adguard-ad-blocker-for-safari/id1047223162) | Safari Block Pop-ups |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stops ad tabs opened with your tap | Yes: a new tab opens only where you pressed | Its listing does not say so | Its listing does not say so | No: a window opened on your tap is allowed |
| Removes invisible layers that catch taps | Yes, before your tap lands | Not listed | Not listed | No |
| Puts back a link rewritten mid-tap | Yes | Not listed | Not listed | No |
| Blocks ads, banners and trackers | Not its job: run it beside 1Blocker or AdGuard | Yes, by filter list | Yes, by filter list | No |
| Shows what a page tried | Every address a page tried to open, blocked or not | Its site says the Mac app shows how many companies tried to track you | Statistics of blocked ads and trackers | Block and Notify on Mac shows a blocked pop-up |
| You decide per site | Allow or block each address, on one site or everywhere | Allowlist a site | Allowlists, blocklists, your own rules | Per website on Mac |
| Works on iPhone, iPad and Mac | Yes | Yes, plus Vision Pro | iPhone and iPad; Mac through AdGuard Mini | Yes |
| No account needed | Yes; no analytics, no server, source public | Yes | Yes; open source | Part of Safari |
| Price | $1.99, paid once, every device | Free for one category; Premium $2.99 a month, $14.99 a year or $39.99 once | Free; Pro sold in the app | Free |

### Two different jobs

A content blocker hands Safari a list of ad and tracker addresses before a page loads, and Safari refuses them. That clears banners and trackers well, and it is why 1Blocker and AdGuard are worth having. It cannot see what a page does with your tap, and pop networks are built around that: the script we took apart in September 2026 did nothing until a real press landed, then spent the press on its own tab. 1Blocker's own listing says "not all ads can be blocked" with Safari's content blocking.

Undirect runs in the page and acts at the moment you press. It removes the layer that would catch the tap, puts back a link that changed while you pressed, and lets a new tab open only where your press pointed. If a redirect rides your tap, the tab is sent back and the address is blocked in Safari, so the next try never loads.

### Undirect and 1Blocker

1Blocker is a polished content blocker for every Apple device, free with one category on at a time and $14.99 a year or $39.99 once for Premium. Keep it for ads and trackers. Add Undirect for the pages that still send you somewhere you did not choose: the two never touch the same thing, so they do not get in each other's way.

### Undirect and AdGuard

AdGuard is free for Safari ad blocking, with Pro sold in the app, and its DNS filtering reaches apps outside Safari. If you already run it and pages still open where you did not tap, that is the part Undirect covers. Undirect's popup lists every address the page tried, so you can see exactly what it stopped and allow anything you want.

### Paid once, for every device

Undirect costs $1.99 once. No subscription and no in-app purchase, and one purchase covers iPhone, iPad and Mac. It runs without an account, analytics or a server, and its [source code](https://github.com/kengomatsuo/undirect) is public. It is off on a site until you press its toolbar button there, so it only acts where you asked it to.

[Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6810513194?pt=127609326&ct=llms&mt=8)

See all seven tools on [Safari pop-up and redirect blockers compared](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/safari-popup-blockers/), read [how to stop Safari redirects on iPhone](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/stop-safari-redirects/), or [try Undirect on the demo sites](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/demo/).

[Apple: Block pop-ups in Safari on iPhone](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/block-pop-ups-ipha49a83ae8/ios); [Apple: Allow or block pop-ups in Safari on Mac](https://support.apple.com/guide/safari/block-pop-ups-sfri40696/mac); [MDN: Window.open()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open); [1Blocker on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/1blocker-ad-blocker/id1365531024) and [1blocker.com](https://1blocker.com/); [AdGuard Ad Blocker for Safari on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/adguard-ad-blocker-for-safari/id1047223162); Undirect's own App Store page. ## Support

One developer answers these.

### Contact

Write to [kenneth@matsuokengo.com](mailto:kenneth@matsuokengo.com).

A site that gets past the guard is more useful as a report. The “Report a site” button in the extension opens a prefilled issue with the details filled in.

### Common problems

**Undirect does not appear in Safari**

Open the app once, then switch Undirect on in Safari's extension settings.

**How do I turn it on for a site?**

Open the site in Safari and press the Undirect button. The guard is off everywhere until you do. Press it again to turn it off for that site.

**A site stopped working after I set a rule**

Press the extension button, find the host and choose its default option. That removes the rule.

**I cannot change rules on iPhone or iPad**

The list in the app is read only there, because iOS gives an app no way to send changes to its own extension. Change rules from the extension button in Safari.

**A window I wanted was blocked**

Its host is in the list. Allow it on that site, or everywhere.

**Why am I still getting pop-ups on Safari?**

Safari's Block Pop-ups only stops windows a page opens without a tap. Most ad pop-ups wait for your tap, so Safari lets them through. Undirect checks whether the tab is what you pressed and stops the ones that are not.

**Is my iPhone hacked or infected?**

Almost always no. A “virus found” or “iPhone at risk” page is an ad the website sent you to. Close the tab and do not install or pay for anything it asks. Undirect stops these when a tap set them off.

**Does it stop redirects that happen without me tapping?**

Yes, from version 1.0.5. On a site where Undirect is on, a page that tries to send you to another site with no tap (on load, on a timer or while you scroll) stays put, and the address shows in Undirect's list so you can allow it if you want.

**Do I still need an ad blocker?**

Undirect does not hide ads on the page. It stops the tabs and redirects that ad blockers miss. Many people run both.

**Is it a subscription?**

No. You pay once and it works on your iPhone, iPad and Mac.

## Privacy

Effective 10 September 2026

No account, no analytics, no server. The list of destinations lives in your browser, and the app reads it through a container on the same machine. Nothing leaves the device unless you press Report, which opens a prefilled issue you send yourself.

### What the extension sees

To catch a click being taken, the guard runs on the sites you switch it on for. It reads the shape of the page: the element under the pointer, where a link points, and which site a new window would go to. None of it is stored or sent.

### What stays on your device

The rules you set, the hosts that were blocked and how many attempts were stopped. They live in Safari's extension storage, and a copy sits in a container that only Undirect and its extension can read, so the app can show the same list. A site switched on from a private window is kept only until the last private tab closes, and never copied for the app.

### Reporting a site

The “Report a site” button opens a prefilled issue on Undirect's public repository at GitHub. It carries the address of the site and what the guard saw there. Nothing is sent until you submit it yourself, and you can edit it or close the tab first. Once submitted it is public, and GitHub's privacy policy applies.

### No third parties

Undirect has no analytics, no advertising code, no crash reporting and no third-party libraries. Blocking uses Safari's own content blocking rules, so the extension never sees the traffic it stops.

### Children and changes

Undirect collects nothing from anyone, of any age. Any change to this page is published here with a new date.

### Contact

Questions go to [kenneth@matsuokengo.com](mailto:kenneth@matsuokengo.com).

## Block Pop-ups is on, and Safari still opens ad pages

The switch is working. The ad pages that get past it come in by other routes, and most of them ride on a tap you made yourself.

Updated 20 November 2026 by Kenneth Fang, who makes Undirect

### Why Block Pop-ups lets them through

Safari's pop-up blocker, like the one in every current browser, stops a window that a page opens on its own. A window opened in direct response to your tap is allowed, because an ordinary link that opens in a new tab works the same way. Mozilla's reference for web developers puts the rule plainly: pop-up windows "must be opened in direct response to user input" ( [MDN, Window.open()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open)).

Ad scripts are written around that rule. We took one pop network's script apart in September 2026, and it did nothing until a real press landed somewhere on the page. Then it spent that press on its own tab, and Safari saw a tab you had asked for.

So the ad pages that reach you with the switch on arrive in one of these ways:

- A tab opened with your tap. The page lays a transparent layer over itself, or listens for any press at all, and opens the ad as if you had clicked a link to it.
- A redirect. The page sends the tab you are reading to another address, which is a trip to a new page and no pop-up at all.
- A swapped link. A link changes its address between the moment your finger lands and the moment it lifts.
- A pop-under. A new tab opens behind the one you are reading, and you find it only when you close the page in front.

### What each Safari setting covers

Every setting here is free and worth turning on. None of them checks what your tap was aimed at, which is the gap the ad pages above use.

| Setting | Where it is | What it stops | What still gets past |
|---|---|---|---|
| Block Pop-ups | iPhone and iPad: Settings, Apps, Safari | A window a page opens without a tap | A tab opened on your tap, a redirect, a swapped link |
| Pop-up Windows | Mac: Safari, Settings, Websites, at the bottom of the list | The same, set per website: Allow, Block, or Block and Notify | The same. Apple adds that blocking pop-ups "might also block some content you want to see" |
| Fraudulent Website Warning | iPhone and iPad: Settings, Apps, Safari. Mac: Safari, Settings, Security | Warns you when you visit a fraudulent website | It warns about a page; it does not stop a tab opening |
| Hide Distracting Items | iPhone: the page menu at the left of the address bar | Menus and other parts of a page that you pick, one by one | Anything you have not picked on that page |
| Extensions | iPhone and iPad: Settings, Apps, Safari, Extensions. Mac: Safari, Settings, Extensions | An extension you do not recognise, once you turn it off | Nothing on its own: it is a list to check |

Sources: [Block pop-ups in Safari on iPhone](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/block-pop-ups-ipha49a83ae8/ios), [Allow or block pop-ups in Safari on Mac](https://support.apple.com/guide/safari/block-pop-ups-sfri40696/mac), [Block pop-up ads and windows in Safari](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102524), [Hide distractions when browsing](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/hide-distractions-when-browsing-iph7778f2888/ios) and [Get extensions](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/get-extensions-iphab0432bf6/ios), all Apple, read 20 November 2026.

### If pop-ups keep coming on a Mac

Apple's Mac guide says that if you block pop-ups on a site and still see them there, you may have unwanted software on the Mac. The steps in Apple's article:

- Update macOS, or restart the Mac if it is already up to date. macOS removes known malware when it restarts.
- Look in the Applications folder for apps you do not remember installing, and delete them.
- In Safari, open Settings, then Extensions, and turn off or remove any extension you do not need.
- To stop Safari reopening last session's windows and tabs, quit it, then hold Shift while you open it again.

Pop-ups on the Lock Screen or in Notification Center are something else: they are notifications from a website you once clicked Allow on. Apple's [article on pop-ups](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102524) links to the steps for managing them on a Mac.

### How to close one safely

Apple warns that some pop-up ads draw a fake close button. If you are not sure, leave the ad alone and close the tab, or type a new address in the search field and go somewhere else. On iPhone, tap the top of the screen if the search field has gone.

### What stops the rest

Undirect watches the tap. On a site where you switch it on, it removes an invisible layer before your tap lands, puts back a link that changed while you pressed, and lets a new tab open only where your press pointed. If a redirect rides your tap, the tab is sent back and that address is blocked in Safari, so the next try never loads. The list in its popup shows every address the page tried, blocked or not. It costs $1.99 once, with no subscription, for iPhone, iPad and Mac.

It pairs with a content blocker such as 1Blocker, AdGuard or Ghostery, which stops known ad and tracker addresses from loading. The two cover different things: 1Blocker's own listing says "not all ads can be blocked", and the ones that get through are the ones Undirect is built for.

[Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6810513194?pt=127609326&ct=llms&mt=8)

Compare [seven pop-up and redirect blockers with prices](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/safari-popup-blockers/), or [try Undirect on the demo sites](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/demo/), made-up pages that misbehave on purpose.

## How to stop Safari opening new tabs by itself

On iPhone, iPad and Mac. The fix depends on what is opening the tabs, and when they appear tells you that.

Updated 20 November 2026 by Kenneth Fang, who makes Undirect

### What is opening the tabs

- A tab that appears right after you tap something on a page, often behind the page you are reading, was opened by the page. When it hides behind, it is called a pop-under.
- Tabs that open with no tap at all, or on every site you visit, point to an extension or, on a Mac, to unwanted software.
- Old tabs that come back when Safari starts are Safari restoring your last session.

### On iPhone and iPad

Open Settings, tap Apps, then Safari, and turn on Block Pop-ups. That stops a page opening a window without a tap.

In the same screen, tap Extensions and read the list. Apple's guide asks you to check the extensions you have installed and make sure you know what they do, so turn off any you do not recognise. To turn one off for a single site, tap the page menu at the left of the address bar in Safari, then Manage Extensions.

Open Links, also under Settings, Apps, Safari, decides what happens to a link you open in a new tab. Apple describes In Background as the way to stay on the current page when you do that. It is a choice about your own links and blocks nothing. Sources: [Block pop-ups](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/block-pop-ups-ipha49a83ae8/ios), [Get extensions](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/get-extensions-iphab0432bf6/ios) and [Open and close tabs](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/open-and-close-tabs-iph489b9313f/ios), Apple's iPhone User Guide.

### On a Mac

In Safari, choose Safari, then Settings, then Websites, and click Pop-up Windows at the bottom of the list on the left. Set "When visiting other websites" to Block, or to Block and Notify if you would like to see what was stopped and open it yourself. A site listed under Configured Websites keeps its own setting.

The Tabs pane has two settings that change where a new tab shows up without stopping it. "Open pages in tabs instead of windows" chooses between a tab and a window. "When a new tab or window opens, make it active" brings the new one to the front; with it off, the new tab stays behind the page you are reading.

If tabs open on their own with no tap, check the Extensions pane in Safari's settings and the Applications folder for anything you did not install, and update macOS, which removes known malware when it restarts. To open Safari without last session's tabs, quit it and hold Shift while you open it again. Sources: [Allow or block pop-ups](https://support.apple.com/guide/safari/block-pop-ups-sfri40696/mac), [Change Tabs settings](https://support.apple.com/guide/safari/tabs-ibrw1045/mac) and [Block pop-up ads and windows in Safari](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102524), Apple, read 20 November 2026.

### Tabs a page opens when you tap

No setting above stops this one. Browsers allow a window opened in direct response to your tap ( [MDN, Window.open()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open)), since a link that opens in a new tab works the same way. A page that waits for your tap can open its ad tab, and Block Pop-ups lets it through.

It takes a Safari extension that knows where your tap was aimed.

Undirect lets a new tab open only where your press pointed, so a tab aimed at an ad is stopped even when your own tap set it off, while the links you open in a new tab and sign-in windows still work. It also removes the invisible layers that catch taps, sends back a redirect that rides one, and lists every address the page tried. It costs $1.99 once for iPhone, iPad and Mac.

Two free extensions handle tabs more bluntly: [Tab Blocker](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tab-blocker/id6759275389) stops every new tab on a site you switch it on for, and [TabGuard](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tabguard/id6756740309) blocks tabs a script opens on its own, while its Smart Mode lets through a tab opened by your click.

[Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6810513194?pt=127609326&ct=llms&mt=8)

Seven options, with prices, are on [Safari pop-up and redirect blockers compared](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/safari-popup-blockers/). You can also [try Undirect on the demo sites](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/demo/) before you buy.

---

Source: https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/safari-popup-blockers/

## Safari pop-up and redirect blockers compared

Most ad pages that get past Safari today ride on a tap you made. Here are seven tools, what each one actually stops, and which to use for the problem you have.

Updated 21 November 2026 by Kenneth Fang, who makes Undirect

| Option | Best for | Price | How it works | Runs on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Undirect (ours) | Taps that land on ad pages, links that change under your finger, tabs you did not open | $1.99 once, one purchase for iPhone, iPad and Mac | Watches each tap and lets the page go only where you pressed | iPhone, iPad, Mac |
| 1Blocker | Ads, trackers and cookie notices | Free for one category; Premium $2.99 a month, $14.99 a year or $39.99 once | Filter lists of known ad and tracker addresses | iPhone, iPad, Mac, Vision Pro |
| AdGuard | Ads, including YouTube, and filtering beyond Safari | Free; Pro sold in the app | Filter lists, plus DNS filtering for other apps | iPhone, iPad; Mac through AdGuard Mini |
| Ghostery | Seeing who tracks you on each site | Free; optional contributions | Filter lists and tracker reports | iPhone, iPad, Mac |
| TabGuard | Tabs a script opens on its own | Free | Blocks new tabs and windows by mode | iPhone, iPad |
| Tab Blocker | A site where you never want a new tab | Free | One switch per site that stops all new tabs | iPhone, iPad |
| Safari's own settings | Windows a page opens with no tap at all | Free, built in | Blocks a window that was not opened by your tap | iPhone, iPad, Mac |

### Which one fits

- Your tap lands on an ad page, a tab opens behind the one you are reading, or a link takes you somewhere it did not say: Undirect. Of the seven listings, it is the only one that says it removes an invisible layer before your tap lands and puts back a link rewritten mid-tap.
- Banners, video ads, trackers or cookie notices are what bother you: a content blocker, 1Blocker, AdGuard or Ghostery.
- One site opens tabs you never want, and you are happy to lose its new-tab links too: Tab Blocker.

A content blocker and Undirect do different jobs, so most people who are tired of ad pages run one of each. Safari's own settings are free and worth switching on whatever else you use.

### Undirect

We make Undirect, a Safari extension for iPhone, iPad and Mac built for the ad pages that come in through your own tap. On a site where you switch it on, it removes an invisible layer before your tap lands, puts back a link rewritten between the press and the release, and lets a new tab open only where your press pointed. Sign-in windows still open, because a window that asks for a size and leads back to the page is let through.

If a redirect rides your tap, the tab is sent back and that address is blocked in Safari, so the next attempt never loads. The popup lists every address the page tried, blocked or not, and you can allow or block each one on that site or everywhere.

It costs $1.99 once: no subscription, no in-app purchase, and one purchase covers iPhone, iPad and Mac. It runs without an account, analytics or a server, and the [source code](https://github.com/kengomatsuo/undirect) is public. It runs on iOS 26.2 and macOS 15 or later, and it works beside whatever content blocker you already use.

[Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6810513194?pt=127609326&ct=llms&mt=8)

You can [try it on the demo sites](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/demo/), made-up pages that misbehave on purpose.

### Why pay when blockers are free

The free tools here are good at what they target. Content blockers stop addresses that are on a list, and Safari stops windows a page opens with no tap. The pop networks we studied wait for a real press and spend it on their own tab, which is the one case neither of those checks ( [MDN: a window opened in response to user input is allowed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open)). Undirect is built for that case, it costs $1.99 once for every device you own, and you never pay again.

### 1Blocker

A well-made content blocker for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Vision Pro, around since 2015. It gives Safari filter lists for ads, more than 50,000 trackers, cookie notices and chat pop-ups, and Safari does the blocking. Free with one category on at a time; Premium is $2.99 a month, $14.99 a year or $39.99 once ( [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/1blocker-ad-blocker/id1365531024), [1blocker.com](https://1blocker.com/)).

Good for: clearing ads and trackers off every site. Its listing says "not all ads can be blocked", since some pages use techniques Safari content blockers cannot reach. A pop script missing from its lists can still spend your tap on an ad tab, and that is where Undirect comes in. [Undirect and 1Blocker side by side](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/compare/#1blocker).

### AdGuard

A content blocker with more than 50 filter lists, and DNS filtering that reaches apps outside Safari. Its listing names banners, pop-ups, autoplay videos, YouTube ads and trackers. Safari blocking is free; Pro adds YouTube blocking, DNS protection and custom rules. On a Mac it is a separate app, [AdGuard Mini](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/adguard-ad-blocker-for-safari/id1440147259) ( [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/adguard-ad-blocker-for-safari/id1047223162), [adguard.com](https://adguard.com/en/adguard-ios/overview.html)).

Good for: ads everywhere, inside Safari and out. Like every filter-list blocker, it acts on addresses it knows, before the page runs; it does not look at where your tap was aimed. [Undirect and AdGuard side by side](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/compare/#adguard).

### Ghostery

A free, open-source blocker for Safari on iPhone, iPad and Mac. Its listing says it blocks ads and pop-ups, YouTube and Facebook included, removes cookie consent pop-ups and shows which trackers each site runs ( [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ghostery-adblocker-for-privacy/id6504861501)).

Good for: seeing and stopping trackers, at no cost. It needs iOS 18.7 or macOS 14.6, and like the other blockers here it works from filter lists rather than from where your tap was aimed.

### TabGuard

A free Safari extension for tabs, with three modes: Block All, Smart Mode, which its listing says allows your clicks and blocks tabs a script opens, and Allow All ( [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tabguard/id6756740309)).

Good for: scripts that open tabs on their own. Smart Mode lets a tab through when your click opened it, and a tab opened with your click is exactly what pop networks wait for. It reached version 1.0 in December 2025.

### Tab Blocker

A free extension that stops a site opening new tabs once you switch it on there, and does nothing elsewhere ( [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tab-blocker/id6759275389)).

Good for: a site where you never want a new tab. It stops every new tab on that site, the links you meant to open in one included.

### Safari's own settings

Block Pop-ups on iPhone and iPad (Settings, Apps, Safari) and Pop-up Windows on a Mac (Safari, Settings, Websites) stop windows a page opens without your tap, and Fraudulent Website Warning flags known fraudulent sites. Turn them on; they cost nothing. A window opened on your tap counts as one you asked for, which is how most ad pages get past them: [why Safari still opens ads with Block Pop-ups on](https://undirect.matsuokengo.com/safari-popups-still-open/).

### A name you may see that is not a blocker

RedirectWeb comes up in searches for a Safari redirect blocker. Its listing describes a URL router that sends links where your rules say, for example Google Maps links to Apple Maps ( [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/redirectweb-smart-url-router/id1571283503)).

### Stop the ad pages that ride your taps

Undirect costs $1.99 once for iPhone, iPad and Mac, and runs beside the blocker you already have.

[Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6810513194?pt=127609326&ct=llms&mt=8)

Sources: each app's own App Store listing and website, and Apple's support pages, read 20 November 2026. Prices are US App Store prices, which differ by country and change.
